sentences.text: Appearance:

Shri Prem Singh Bhadouria - Advocate for the petitio  Shri Sohit Mishra - GA appearing on behalf of State.
 Shri Sooraj Bhan Lodhi, learned counsel for the resp  ORDER Case Diary is perused.
2. Learned counsel for the rival parties are heard.
3. The applicant has filed this 2nd repeat bail application u/S 439, Cr.P.C/Section 483 of BNSS for grant of bail.

The applicant has been arrested on 31.05.2024 by Police Station Bhauti, District Shivpuri in connection with Crime No.96/2024 registered in relation to the offences punishable u/Ss. 376(3), 342, 294, 323, 506 of IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act.

4. This second repeat bail application has been filed after dismissal of the earlier application on merits vide order dated 14.11.2024 in M.Cr.C.No.35340/2024.
5.

The present application has been moved on the pretext that after dismissal of the first bail application, DNA report which was not filed along with challan has been submitted before the Trial Court, wherein a negative report has been received which implies that the present applicant had not committed rape on NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:468 2 MCRC-54901-2024 the prosecutrix.

sentences.text: Another ground which has been raised is that just two days prior to the dismissal of the earlier application, the statements of the prosecutrix were recorded and that could not be brought before this Court since it was not in the knowledge of the counsel and in the said statements contradictory material has come on record which also goes to show that the case of the prosecution could not be prima facie established against the present applicant.

7. Another ground which has been raised is that the statement of landlord of the house in which prosecutrix was living had been recorded who is stated to have been narrated the incident by the father of the prosecutrix and after that the FIR was lodged, had turned hostile.

It has also been argued that the present applicant has falsely been implicated in the incident as father of the prosecutrix is working under a person who is an accused in a crime related to murder of the brother of the present applicant, therefore, just to pressurize the present applicant, the said FIR has been registered.
In the aforesaid premise the second bail application has been filed.

8. On the other hand, this bail application has been opposed by the learned Government Advocate as well advocate for the complainant and it has been stated that firstly the earlier bail application has been dismissed on merits, wherein all the arguments as advanced had already been considered.

At the time of dismissal of the first bail application the statements of the prosecutrix were already available though not placed before this Court, but in the statements, she has very well supported the case of the prosecution.

It was also argued that the counsel for the applicant though had tried to harp upon the contradictions in the statements of the prosecutirix in the cross-examination, but the said contradictions cannot be NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:468 3 MCRC-54901-2024 adjudicated while deciding the bail petition and it is the prerogative and domain of the learned Trial Court to adjudicate the same and, thereafter, take any decision.

It was further submitted that in the month of May, 2024, the DNA report was already available with the learned Trial Court and formed part of the charge-sheet and only thereafter the first bail application has been rejected.

Thus, it was prayed that the present application is devoid of any merits, therefore, is liable to be dismissed.
9.

After hearing the rival contentions, this Court finds that once the prosecutrix has supported the case of the prosecution and even though there are contradictions in her statement, this Court while adjudicating the bail application cannot go on to appreciate the statements made by the prosecutrix which is to be done by the learned Trial Court at the time of final adjudication.

10. So far as the other aspects as argued by the learned counsel for the applicant are concerned, they were available at the time of dismissal of the first application on merits and were appreciated,
therefore, no case for bail is made out.
11. Accordingly, this second bail application is also hereby dismissed.

(MILIND RAMESH PHADKE) JUDGE Chandni Sanju@Sanjeev vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163704649/
